intro.title: Generic useFetch<T>
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable Angular service called `useFetch<T>` that fetches data from an API. You'll learn how to use TypeScript generics, denoted by `<T>`, to make this service work with any data type, ensuring type safety. The main technologies involved are Angular's HttpClient for making HTTP requests and RxJS Observables for handling asynchronous data streams. By the end, you'll have a flexible service that can fetch and return typed data for different endpoints in your application.
intro.usecase: In real-world Angular applications, a generic `useFetch<T>` pattern is essential for building dynamic data-driven interfaces. For example, an e-commerce dashboard might use it to fetch and display various data types—like `Product[]` for inventory listings, `Order[]` for recent sales, or `User[]` for customer management—all with a single reusable service. This approach streamlines development in admin panels, analytics tools, and content management systems, where consistent data fetching logic is needed across multiple components handling different API resources.
